label: Asymmetric existential requirement inside the full effect first cause
term: asymmetric existential requirement in the full effect first cause
definition: Prior requirement x y := requirement x y and not requirement y x. The primitive requirement x y means that y requires x in order to exist. The asymmetry is a transparent definition; requirement itself has no supplied reduction to modal implication, production or parthood.
note: Analyst formal reconstruction of the existing existential-requirement reading, with historical attribution deferred. It makes the asymmetric component explicit without pretending that the old cause-to-effect-part policy defines requirement. A component/whole existential dependence is an illustrative candidate, not an independently certified instance; reciprocal co-dependence supplies neither direction of Prior. Temporal priority, part overlap and partial productive participation are insufficient. Asymmetry and irreflexivity of Prior follow from the body; transitivity of requirement or Prior, well-foundedness, real applicability and production/parthood bridges remain OPEN. A Humean account may reject real existential requirement; mutual-dependence accounts can accept requirement while denying either asymmetric direction. No new source claim or independent metaphysical warrant is asserted.
